events.title: BlackBerry 7290 released
events.summary: BlackBerry released the BlackBerry 7290 — Bluetooth and color screen enterprise BlackBerry.
events.about: BlackBerry dominated enterprise mobile before iPhone and Android. Bluetooth and color screen enterprise blackberry. BES-connected apps and push email defined mobile workflows for years.

narrative.whyChosen: The BlackBerry 7290 was a key BlackBerry hardware milestone.
narrative.whyImportant: BlackBerry hardware set expectations for mobile email and messaging security.
narrative.problemSolved: Business users needed secure mobile email before modern smartphone platforms.

events.title: Selenium released
events.summary: Jason Huggins open sourced Selenium at ThoughtWorks in 2004 — a JavaScript-based framework for automating browser tests.
events.about: Selenium drove browsers from HTML tables of commands — click, type, assert — before dedicated WebDriver binaries existed. It became the default way QA teams regression-tested web apps and later merged with WebDriver into Selenium 2. Cypress and Playwright are spiritual successors with modern APIs.

narrative.whyChosen: Selenium pioneered open-source browser test automation for the web era.
narrative.whyImportant: It established keyword-driven testing patterns used across the industry for a decade.
narrative.problemSolved: Manual clicking through web apps for every release did not scale as Agile teams shipped faster.

events.title: Shopware first released
events.summary: Stefan and Sebastian Hamann released Shopware version 1 in 2004 — a modular PHP e-commerce platform developed in Germany.
events.about: Shopware grew from Hamann-Media's agency work into a standalone product — templates, checkout, and catalog management for European merchants. It later open-sourced its Community Edition and rebuilt as Shopware 6 on Symfony and Vue.js.

narrative.whyChosen: Shopware became Europe's leading open-source e-commerce platform.
narrative.whyImportant: It gave DACH-region merchants a PHP alternative to Magento and proprietary carts.
narrative.problemSolved: European retailers lacked flexible, locally supported e-commerce software.
